title: Give each component exactly one business capability

facts.note: Task text mentions components, their names or responsibilities.
Any planner-authored artifact that declares, describes or references a component; the rule applies to every component, new or existing.

Whether a component bundles several capabilities, whether its name reflects its primary business purpose, and whether the name follows {business-capability}-{layer-role} are semantic judgements; implementation.type is none, so no detector exists. A pattern-shape check could become a new observer but the capability meaning still needs judgement.

fires: Planner declares a new component and chooses its responsibility and name.
Planner renames, re-scopes or describes an existing component.

Planner authors or reviews any plan, wagon, WMBT, acceptance or doc in which a component (new or pre-existing) appears whose responsibility spans several business capabilities, whose name does not reflect its purpose, or whose name does not follow {business-capability}-{layer-role}.
doesNotFire: Planner artifacts that neither declare, describe nor reference any component.
Counting methods on a component (covered by planner.component.method-limit).

given: A planner artifact declares, describes or references a component (new or existing)
when: the planner defines or evaluates that component's responsibility
then: Ensure the component has exactly one business capability.
prefer: Pick the single capability from the canonical vocabulary a component name can express — core business: validator (validates business rules and constraints), processor (processes business logic and computations), coordinator (coordinates multiple operations), transformer (transforms data between formats), aggregator (aggregates data from multiple sources); UI/UX: display (displays information to users), collector (collects user input), navigator (manages navigation flow); integration: persister (persists data to storage), fetcher (fetches data from external sources), publisher (publishes events/notifications), subscriber (subscribes to events/notifications).
Compliant names: option-validator, decision-processor, dilemma-display, choice-persister, result-publisher.
avoid: Components whose responsibility spans several business capabilities, or that hide the mix behind a generic word.
REQUIRED, not optional: a component name that does not reflect its primary business purpose. Check this separately from the single-capability check; passing one does not pass the other.
REQUIRED, not optional: a component name that does not follow the pattern {business-capability}-{layer-role}. A name that reflects the purpose but breaks the pattern is still non-compliant.
Vague catch-all names with no single business capability, such as manager-helper-util.
why: One business capability per component keeps responsibilities sharp and makes the component's name a faithful index of what it does, so the graph stays readable and components stay swappable.
evidence: Reviewer reads each component's described responsibility and confirms it maps to exactly one business capability.
Reviewer separately confirms each component's name reflects that primary business purpose.
Reviewer separately confirms each component's name follows {business-capability}-{layer-role} (capability term e.g. from the canonical vocabulary).
verifier_detail: No automated detector (implementation.type: none); compliance is judged by review.
Naming pattern (mandatory): {business-capability}-{layer-role}. Source: 'Component names follow the pattern {business-capability}-{layer-role}.'

Capability vocabulary (canonical capabilities a component name can express; source does not state it is exhaustive) — core_business: validator, processor, coordinator, transformer, aggregator; ui_ux: display, collector, navigator; integration: persister, fetcher, publisher, subscriber. Meanings as listed in prefer[0].
Source examples (compliant): option-validator, decision-processor, dilemma-display, choice-persister, result-publisher.
Source counter-example: manager-helper-util — vague, no single business capability.

Check (term single_capability): rule 'Each component must have single business capability'; check 'Component name reflects its primary business purpose'. Treat the capability, purpose-reflecting name and naming-pattern checks as three independent pass/fail items.

additions.text: 'then' keeps only the single-capability obligation (S006 first clause, S019).
